| summarize ClosedUniqueIncidents = count() by Month
| order by Month asc

name: Yearly Responder Breakdown by Incident Type
desc: Annual breakdown of closed incidents per responder and incident title. Shows which analysts handled which detection rules over the full year. Useful for annual performance reviews and workload distribution analysis.
kql:
// NOTE: Adjust start and end dates to your reporting period
let start = datetime(2025-01-01);
let end   = datetime(2026-01-01);
SecurityIncident
| where TimeGenerated >= start and TimeGenerated < end
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| where Status == "Closed" and isnotempty(ClosedTime)
| where ClosedTime >= start and ClosedTime < end
| extend Month = format_datetime(ClosedTime, "yyyy-MM")
| extend ResponderRaw = coalesce(tostring(Owner.assignedTo), tostring(Owner.userPrincipalName))
| where isnotempty(ResponderRaw) and ResponderRaw !in~ ("Unassigned")
| extend Responder = iff(ResponderRaw contains "@", tostring(split(ResponderRaw, "@")[0]), ResponderRaw)
| summarize ClosedIncidents = dcount(IncidentNumber) by Month, Responder, Title
| order by Month asc, Responder asc, ClosedIncidents desc

name: Single Responder Monthly Trend
desc: Tracks a specific responder's monthly closed incident count over a year. Useful for individual performance tracking and 1:1 review preparation.
kql:
// NOTE: Replace accountid with the responder's account name and adjust dates
let start = datetime(2025-01-01);
let end   = datetime(2026-01-01);
let responder = "accountid";
SecurityIncident
| where Status == "Closed"
| where isnotempty(CreatedTime) and isnotempty(ClosedTime)
| where ClosedTime >= start and ClosedTime < end
| extend Month = format_datetime(ClosedTime, "yyyy-MM")
| extend ResponderRaw = coalesce(tostring(Owner.assignedTo), tostring(Owner.userPrincipalName))
| where isnotempty(ResponderRaw) and ResponderRaw !in~ ("Unassigned")
| extend Responder = iff(ResponderRaw contains "@", tostring(split(ResponderRaw, "@")[0]), ResponderRaw)
| where Responder =~ responder
| summarize ClosedCount = count() by Month
| order by Month asc

name: Top 10 Closed Incident Types
desc: Shows the top 10 most frequently closed incident types (by title/detection rule name). Helps identify which detections generate the most work and may be candidates for automation or tuning.

name: Yearly Responder MTTR Performance
desc: Annual MTTR performance per responder with closed count, average/P50/P90 resolution times. Designed for year-end SOC performance reviews and identifying training needs.
kql:
// NOTE: Adjust start and end dates to your reporting period
let monthStart = datetime(2025-01-01);
let monthEnd   = datetime(2026-01-01);
SecurityIncident
| where Status == "Closed"
| where isnotempty(CreatedTime) and isnotempty(ClosedTime)
| where ClosedTime >= monthStart and ClosedTime < monthEnd
| extend ResponderRaw = coalesce(tostring(Owner.assignedTo), tostring(Owner.userPrincipalName))
| where isnotempty(ResponderRaw) and ResponderRaw !in~ ("Unassigned")
| extend Responder = iff(ResponderRaw contains "@", tostring(split(ResponderRaw, "@")[0]), ResponderRaw)
| extend ResolveMinutes = (ClosedTime - CreatedTime) / 1m
| summarize
    ClosedCount = count(),
    MTTR_Min = avg(ResolveMinutes),
    P50_Min  = percentile(ResolveMinutes, 50),
    P90_Min  = percentile(ResolveMinutes, 90)
  by Responder
| order by ClosedCount desc

name: OAuth Consent and App Registration Summary
desc: Summarizes all OAuth consent grants, app role assignments, permission grants, new app registrations and service principal additions over 7 days. Shows which apps received consent, how many times and by whom. Broader than illicit consent detection. Covers all consent activity for governance review.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has_any ("Consent to application", "Add app role assignment", "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant", "Add application", "Add service principal")
| extend InitiatedBy = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend TargetApp = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend TargetAppId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| summarize 
    ConsentCount = count(),
    LastConsent = max(TimeGenerated),
    Users = make_set(InitiatedBy, 10)
    by OperationName, TargetApp, TargetAppId
| order by ConsentCount desc

name: Active Account Password Age Report
desc: Password age report for accounts that are not disabled, combining the IdentityAccountInfo and IdentityInfo tables. Shows days and years since last password change, PasswordNeverExpires and PasswordNotRequired flags, sensitive account tagging and OU path. The two tables are joined on AccountUpn, so accounts without a UPN are not listed. Hunting query, not an alert. Requires MDI. The join key was changed after a schema check and the query has not been run against live data.
kql:
let accountinfo = IdentityAccountInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(AccountUpn)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by IdentityId
| extend DaysSinceLastPasswordChange =
    iff(isnull(LastPasswordChangeTime), long(null),
        datetime_diff('day', now(), LastPasswordChangeTime))
| extend YearsSinceLastPasswordChange =
    iff(isnull(LastPasswordChangeTime), long(null),
        datetime_diff('year', now(), LastPasswordChangeTime))
| extend Sensitive = array_index_of(Tags, "Sensitive") != -1
| extend SensitiveLabel = iff(Sensitive, "Sensitive", "Not Sensitive")
| project AccountUpn, AccountStatus, LastPasswordChangeTime, DaysSinceLastPasswordChange, YearsSinceLastPasswordChange, Sid, Sensitive, SensitiveLabel;
let IdInfo = IdentityInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(AccountUpn)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AccountObjectId
| extend PasswordNeverExpires = UserAccountControl has "PasswordNeverExpires",
         PasswordNotRequired = UserAccountControl has "PasswordNotRequired"
| extend OUPath = extract(@"CN=[^,]+,(.*)", 1, DistinguishedName)
| project AccountObjectId, AccountName, AccountDomain, AccountDisplayName, OnPremSid, OnPremObjectId, AccountUpn, PasswordNeverExpires, PasswordNotRequired, Type, OUPath;
IdInfo
| join kind=leftouter (accountinfo) on AccountUpn
| where AccountStatus != "Disabled"
| project AccountObjectId, AccountName, AccountStatus, AccountDomain, AccountDisplayName, AccountUpn, Sensitive, SensitiveLabel, LastPasswordChangeTime, DaysSinceLastPasswordChange, YearsSinceLastPasswordChange, PasswordNeverExpires, PasswordNotRequired, Type, OUPath
| sort by DaysSinceLastPasswordChange desc

name: Password Age Distribution by Bucket
desc: Groups accounts that are not disabled into password age buckets (0-1 years, 1-2 years, 2-5 years, 5-10 years, 10+ years). Gives a quick view of password hygiene across the organization. The IdentityAccountInfo and IdentityInfo tables are joined on AccountUpn, so accounts without a UPN are not counted. Hunting query, not an alert. Requires MDI. The join key was changed after a schema check and the query has not been run against live data.
kql:
let accountinfo = IdentityAccountInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(AccountUpn)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by IdentityId
| extend DaysSinceLastPasswordChange =
    iff(isnull(LastPasswordChangeTime), long(null),
        datetime_diff('day', now(), LastPasswordChangeTime))
| project AccountUpn, AccountStatus, LastPasswordChangeTime, DaysSinceLastPasswordChange;
let IdInfo = IdentityInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(AccountUpn)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AccountObjectId
| project AccountObjectId, AccountUpn;
IdInfo
| join kind=leftouter (accountinfo) on AccountUpn
| where AccountStatus != "Disabled"
| where isnotnull(LastPasswordChangeTime)
| extend PasswordAgeBucket =
    case(
        DaysSinceLastPasswordChange <= 365, "0-1 years",
        DaysSinceLastPasswordChange <= 2*365, "1-2 years",
        DaysSinceLastPasswordChange <= 5*365, "2-5 years",
        DaysSinceLastPasswordChange <= 10*365, "5-10 years",
        "10+ years")
| summarize Accounts = dcount(AccountObjectId) by PasswordAgeBucket
| sort by Accounts desc

name: ChatGPT Enterprise Sign-In Monitoring
desc: Monitors sign-in activity to the ChatGPT Enterprise application (AppID: e0476654-c1d5-430b-ab80-70cbd947616a) over 180 days. Shows which users accessed it, from where, how Conditional Access evaluated the attempt and whether MFA was required. Useful for AI governance reviews.
kql:
let ChatGPTAppId = "e0476654-c1d5-430b-ab80-70cbd947616a";
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(180d)
| where AppId == ChatGPTAppId
| extend
    Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion),
    City    = tostring(LocationDetails.city)
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    UserDisplayName,
    UserPrincipalName,
    IPAddress,
    Country,
    City,
    ConditionalAccessStatus,
    ClientAppUsed,
    AuthenticationRequirement,
    ResultType,
    ResultDescription
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Entra ID Admin Role Assignments
desc: Lists users with Entra ID admin role assignments seen in the last 30 days. Shows which accounts hold which administrative roles. Useful for privileged access reviews and for finding over-privileged accounts.
kql:
IdentityInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AssignedRoles != ""
| mv-expand AssignedRoles
| extend EntraAdminRole = tostring(AssignedRoles)
| project Timestamp, EntraAdminRole, AccountDisplayName
| where AccountDisplayName != ""
| sort by EntraAdminRole asc, Timestamp desc

name: Weak MFA Method Registration Detection
desc: Detects when users register or are configured with weak MFA methods: voice call (mobile/office/other), SMS (two-way/one-way). These methods are vulnerable to SIM swapping, SS7 attacks and social engineering. Any registration of weak methods should be investigated. Could indicate an attacker downgrading MFA to bypass stronger methods.
kql:
let WeakMethods = dynamic([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
let WeakMethodNames = dynamic(["TwoWayVoiceMobile","TwoWaySms","TwoWayVoiceOffice","TwoWayVoiceOtherMobile","TwoWaySmsOtherMobile","OneWaySms"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "Update user."
| where RawEventData contains "StrongAuthenticationMethod"
| extend Target = tostring(RawEventData.ObjectId)
| extend Actor = tostring(RawEventData.UserId)
| mv-expand ModifiedProperties = parse_json(RawEventData.ModifiedProperties)
| where ModifiedProperties.Name == "StrongAuthenticationMethod"
| extend NewValue = parse_json(tostring(ModifiedProperties.NewValue))
| mv-apply NewValue on (
    extend MethodType = toint(NewValue.MethodType)
    | where MethodType in (WeakMethods)
    | summarize AddedWeakMethods = make_set(strcat(MethodType, ": ", iff(MethodType < array_length(WeakMethodNames), tostring(WeakMethodNames[MethodType]), "Unknown")))
)
| where array_length(AddedWeakMethods) > 0
| extend AddedWeakMethodsStr = tostring(AddedWeakMethods)
| project Timestamp, Actor, Target, AddedWeakMethodsStr, ReportId
| distinct *
| order by Timestamp desc

name: Sensitive Accounts List (Exposure Graph)
desc: Lists all user accounts tagged as Sensitive in Microsoft Security Exposure Management, along with their nested AD group memberships. Sensitive accounts are high-value targets. This query helps verify the sensitive account list is accurate and complete.
kql:
ExposureGraphNodes
| where NodeLabel == 'user'
| extend Tags = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(tostring(NodeProperties.rawData)).tags.[0]))
| extend NestedADGroups = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(tostring(NodeProperties.rawData)).nestedAdGroupNames))
| mv-expand NestedADGroups
| where Tags == 'Sensitive'

name: Temporary Access Pass (TAP) Usage
desc: Tracks all Temporary Access Pass creation and usage events. TAPs are time-limited credentials used for onboarding or recovery. Unauthorized TAP creation could indicate an attacker bypassing standard authentication to gain access to an account.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where Result == "success"
| where ResultDescription has "temporary access pass"
| project TimeGenerated, ResultDescription, OperationName, Identity, InitiatedBy, TargetResources
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: User URL Click Investigation
desc: Investigates all URLs clicked by specific target users that were allowed through Safe Links. Shows URL domains, click counts and timestamps. Useful for post-incident investigation when you need to know exactly what a compromised user clicked on.
kql:
// NOTE: Replace account@domain.com with the user(s) you want to investigate
let TargetUsers = dynamic(["account@domain.com"]);
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountUpn in~ (TargetUsers)
| where ActionType == "ClickAllowed"
| extend UrlDomain = extract("https?://([^/]+)", 1, Url)
| summarize 
    ClickedBy = make_set(AccountUpn),
    ClickedByCount = dcount(AccountUpn),
    ClickTimes = make_set(Timestamp),
    TotalClicks = count()
    by Url, UrlDomain, NetworkMessageId
| order by ClickedByCount desc, TotalClicks desc

name: Privileged Account Authentication Posture Audit
desc: Audits the authentication posture of highly privileged Entra ID accounts over 30 days using Defender XDR Advanced Hunting. Identifies privileged users across a full tiered admin role list (Tier 0/1/2) and assesses sign-in activity: total sign-ins, MFA vs single-factor sign-in counts, unique IPs, unique apps and inactive privileged accounts. Each account gets a risk indicator flagging single-factor sign-ins present, no sign-ins in 30 days, or OK. Note: unlike the Sentinel SigninLogs table, EntraIdSignInEvents does not expose a breakdown by authentication method (no FIDO2, SMS or password breakdown), so this version relies on the AuthenticationRequirement field (MFA vs single-factor) as the primary signal.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
let PrivilegedRoles = dynamic([
// ===== ENTRA TIER 0 (Critical - Tenant-Control) =====
	"Global Administrator",
	"Privileged Role Administrator",
	"Privileged Authentication Administrator",
	"Security Administrator",
	"Conditional Access Administrator",
	"Application Administrator",
	"Cloud Application Administrator",
	"Hybrid Identity Administrator",
	"Partner Tier2 Support",
// ===== ENTRA TIER 1 (High - Service-Control/ Writepermission) =====
	"Authentication Administrator",
	"Authentication Policy Administrator",
	"Authentication Extensibility Administrator",
	"User Administrator",
	"Helpdesk Administrator",
	"Password Administrator",
	"Directory Writers",
	"Directory Synchronization Accounts",
	"Domain Name Administrator",
	"External Identity Provider Administrator",
	"Lifecycle Workflows Administrator",
	"Groups Administrator",
	"Identity Governance Administrator",
	"Exchange Administrator",
	"SharePoint Administrator",
	"Teams Administrator",
	"Teams Telephony Administrator",
	"Skype for Business Administrator",
	"Intune Administrator",
	"Compliance Administrator",
	"Security Operator",
	"Power Platform Administrator",
	"Dynamics 365 Administrator",
	"AI Administrator",
	"Global Secure Access Administrator",
	"Attribute Assignment Administrator",
	"Attribute Provisioning Administrator",
	"B2C IEF Keyset Administrator",
	"Cloud App Security Administrator",
	"External ID User Flow Administrator",
	"Partner Tier1 Support",
	"Windows 365 Administrator",
	"Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator",
	"Microsoft 365 Migration Administrator",
	"Yammer Administrator",
	"Knowledge Administrator",
	"Billing Administrator",
// ===== ENTRA TIER 2 (Medium - Read-only / restricted) =====
	"Global Reader",
	"Security Reader",
	"Attribute Provisioning Reader",
	"Application Developer",
	"Cloud Device Administrator",
	"Azure AD Joined Device Local Administrator",
	"Microsoft Entra Joined Device Local Administrator"
]);
let PrivilegedUsers =
	IdentityInfo
	| where Timestamp >= ago(Lookback)
	| where AssignedRoles has_any (PrivilegedRoles)
	| summarize
		AssignedRoles  = make_set(AssignedRoles),
		Department	 = take_any(Department),
		JobTitle	   = take_any(JobTitle),
		AccountEnabled = take_any(IsAccountEnabled)
		by AccountUpn;
let AuthEvents =
	EntraIdSignInEvents
	| where Timestamp >= ago(Lookback)
	| where ErrorCode == 0
	| summarize
		TotalSignins		= count(),
		LastSignin			= max(Timestamp),
		UniqueIPs			= dcount(IPAddress),
		UniqueApps			= dcount(Application),
		MFASignins			= countif(AuthenticationRequirement == "multiFactorAuthentication"),
		SingleFactorSignins	= countif(AuthenticationRequirement == "singleFactorAuthentication")
		by AccountUpn;
PrivilegedUsers
| join kind=leftouter AuthEvents
	on $left.AccountUpn == $right.AccountUpn
| project
	User				= AccountUpn,
	Roles				= AssignedRoles,
	AccountActive		= AccountEnabled,
	SigninCount			= coalesce(TotalSignins, 0),
	MFASignins			= coalesce(MFASignins, 0),
	SingleFactorSignins	= coalesce(SingleFactorSignins, 0),
	LastSignin			= LastSignin,
	UniqueIPs			= coalesce(UniqueIPs, 0),
	UniqueApps			= coalesce(UniqueApps, 0),
	RiskIndicator		= case(
		coalesce(SingleFactorSignins, 0) > 0, "Single-factor sign-ins present",
		coalesce(TotalSignins, 0) == 0,	   "No sign-ins in 30 days",
											  "OK"
	)
| sort by SigninCount desc

name: New AI Agent Created With Excessive Org-Wide Sharing
desc: Detects newly created AI agents (within the last 2 days) that were configured with org-wide sharing (shared with everyone in the tenant) while also having MCP servers or declared tools attached. A brand new agent with both broad capabilities and org-wide visibility is a governance red flag, since it means anyone in the tenant can invoke an agent with tool access before it has been reviewed.
kql:
let lookback = 14d;
let recent = 2d;
let FirstSnapshot = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| summarize arg_min(Timestamp, *) by AgentId;
FirstSnapshot
| where CreatedDateTime > ago(recent)
| extend McpServerCount = array_length(coalesce(McpServers, dynamic([])))
| extend DeclaredToolCount = array_length(coalesce(DeclaredTools, dynamic([])))
| extend OwnerCount = array_length(coalesce(Owners, dynamic([])))
| extend IsOrgWide = set_has_element(coalesce(SharedWith, dynamic([])), "*")
| where (McpServerCount > 0 or DeclaredToolCount > 0) and IsOrgWide
| project AgentId, Name, Platform, CreatedDateTime, McpServerCount, DeclaredToolCount, OwnerCount, IsOrgWide
| sort by CreatedDateTime desc

name: Agent Configuration and Access Policy Tampering Detection
desc: Compares each AI agent's current state with its 14-day baseline to find configuration drift: instructions changed, a new MCP server added, an owner added or sharing expanded to org-wide. Flags agents where 2 or more of these signals occurred together, because a single change can be routine maintenance but several at once can point to deliberate tampering. MITRE ATLAS: AML.T0081 (Modify AI Agent Configuration).
kql:
let lookback = 14d;
let recent = 2d;
let CurrentMcpNames = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(recent)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| mv-expand Mcp = McpServers
| extend McpName = tostring(Mcp.name)
| where isnotempty(McpName)
| summarize CurrentMcpServers = make_set(McpName) by AgentId;
let BaselineMcpNames = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp between (ago(lookback) .. ago(recent))
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| mv-expand Mcp = McpServers
| extend McpName = tostring(Mcp.name)
| where isnotempty(McpName)
| summarize BaselineMcpServers = make_set(McpName) by AgentId;
let CurrentState = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(recent)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| project AgentId, Name, Platform, Timestamp,
    CurrentInstructions = Instructions,
    CurrentOwners = Owners,
    CurrentSharedWith = SharedWith;
let BaselineState = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp between (ago(lookback) .. ago(recent))
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| project AgentId,
    PreviousInstructions = Instructions,
    PreviousOwners = Owners,
    BaselineSharedWith = SharedWith;
let Joined = CurrentState
| join kind=inner (BaselineState) on AgentId
| join kind=leftouter (CurrentMcpNames) on AgentId
| join kind=leftouter (BaselineMcpNames) on AgentId;
let InstructionsFlag = Joined
| where CurrentInstructions != PreviousInstructions
| project AgentId, Signal = "InstructionsChanged";
let McpFlag = Joined
| where array_length(set_difference(coalesce(CurrentMcpServers, dynamic([])), coalesce(BaselineMcpServers, dynamic([])))) > 0
| project AgentId, Signal = "NewMcpServer";
let OwnerFlag = Joined
| where array_length(set_difference(CurrentOwners, PreviousOwners)) > 0
| project AgentId, Signal = "OwnerAdded";
let SharingFlag = Joined
| where set_has_element(coalesce(CurrentSharedWith, dynamic([])), "*")
| where not(set_has_element(coalesce(BaselineSharedWith, dynamic([])), "*"))
| project AgentId, Signal = "SharingExpandedOrgWide";
union InstructionsFlag, McpFlag, OwnerFlag, SharingFlag
| summarize SignalCount = dcount(Signal), Signals = make_set(Signal) by AgentId
| where SignalCount >= 2
| join kind=inner (CurrentState) on AgentId
| project AgentId, Name, Platform, SignalCount, Signals, Timestamp
| sort by SignalCount desc

name: New Owner Role Assignment at Subscription Scope
desc: Detects when a user is granted the Owner role at subscription scope via Azure Activity Log. Owner role grants full control including the ability to assign roles to others. Subscription-scope Owner assignments outside change management are a critical privilege escalation indicator.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue =~ 'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| extend RoleAssignmentProps = parse_json(Properties)
| extend RequestBody = parse_json(tostring(RoleAssignmentProps.requestbody))
| extend RoleDefinitionId = tostring(RequestBody.Properties.RoleDefinitionId)
| where RoleDefinitionId has '8e3af657-a8ff-443c-a75c-2fe8c4bcb635' // built-in Owner role GUID
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId, RoleDefinitionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: PIM Privileged Role Activation Monitoring
desc: Tracks all Privileged Identity Management (PIM) role activations from Entra ID audit logs. Shows who activated which role, when and from what IP. Establishes a baseline of normal PIM usage and helps identify off-hours activations or activations without expected justification.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Category == 'RoleManagement'
| where ActivityDisplayName == 'Add member to role completed (PIM activation)'
| extend Actor = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend ActorIP = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.ipAddress)
| extend Role = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| extend Hour = datetime_part('Hour', TimeGenerated)
| extend IsOffHours = Hour < 7 or Hour > 19
| project TimeGenerated, Actor, Role, ActorIP, IsOffHours, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Direct Privileged Role Assignment Bypassing PIM
desc: Detects direct (permanent) privileged role assignments in Entra ID that bypass PIM just-in-time activation. Permanent Global Administrator or other Tier 0 role assignments outside PIM indicate either a misconfiguration or an attacker with Directory.Write permissions establishing persistent access.
kql:
// NOTE: Adjust PrivilegedRoles list to match your Tier 0 roles
let PrivilegedRoles = dynamic(['Global Administrator', 'Privileged Role Administrator', 'Security Administrator', 'Application Administrator']);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Category == 'RoleManagement'
| where ActivityDisplayName == 'Add member to role'
| extend Role = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| where Role in (PrivilegedRoles)
| extend Actor = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend TargetUser = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, Actor, TargetUser, Role, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: User Added to Privileged Group
desc: Detects when a user is added to a security group that grants elevated privileges (role-assignable groups or groups matching admin naming patterns). Attackers use privileged group membership as a stealthier persistence mechanism than direct role assignment since group changes are reviewed less often.
kql:
// NOTE: Adjust PrivilegedGroupNames to match your tenant's admin group naming convention
let PrivilegedGroupNames = dynamic(['Admin', 'Global Admins', 'Privileged', 'Security Admins', 'Domain Admins']);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName == 'Add member to group'
| extend GroupName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| where GroupName has_any (PrivilegedGroupNames)
| extend Actor = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend AddedUser = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[1].userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, Actor, AddedUser, GroupName, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Large Blob Download from Storage Account
desc: Detects unusually large blob download volumes from Azure Storage accounts within a short window. A single caller downloading gigabytes of blob data in a short period is a strong indicator of data exfiltration, especially from storage accounts holding sensitive backups or database exports.
kql:
StorageBlobLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationName == 'GetBlob'
| where StatusCode == 200
| summarize TotalBytes = sum(ResponseBodySize), RequestCount = count(), Blobs = make_set(Uri, 10)
    by CallerIpAddress, AccountName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| extend TotalMB = round(TotalBytes / 1048576.0, 1)
| where TotalMB > 500
| order by TotalMB desc

name: Bulk Storage Read Operations
desc: Detects a high volume of read operations (list, get) against a storage account from a single caller. Bulk enumeration followed by mass reads often precedes exfiltration and can also indicate a misconfigured or compromised automation identity scanning storage for sensitive files.
kql:
StorageBlobLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationName in ('GetBlob', 'ListBlobs', 'GetBlobProperties')
| summarize ReadOps = count(), UniqueBlobs = dcount(Uri) by CallerIpAddress, AccountName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where ReadOps > 500
| order by ReadOps desc

name: Guest User Invited to Tenant
desc: Tracks all guest user invitations sent to external identities. Shows who invited whom, from which domain and whether the invite was accepted. Establishes a baseline of expected B2B collaboration and helps catch invitations to unexpected or personal email domains.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName == 'Invite external user'
| extend InvitedBy = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend InvitedEmail = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].userPrincipalName)
| extend InvitedDomain = tolower(tostring(split(InvitedEmail, '@')[-1]))
| project TimeGenerated, InvitedBy, InvitedEmail, InvitedDomain, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: App Registration Redirect URI Modified
desc: Detects when the redirect URI of an app registration is modified. Attackers who compromise an application owner account can add a redirect URI pointing to attacker-controlled infrastructure, silently redirecting OAuth authorization codes and tokens to themselves.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName == 'Update application'
| extend ModifiedProps = parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].modifiedProperties
| mv-expand ModifiedProps
| where tostring(ModifiedProps.displayName) has 'RedirectUri'
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| extend ModifiedBy = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend OldValue = tostring(ModifiedProps.oldValue)
| extend NewValue = tostring(ModifiedProps.newValue)
| project TimeGenerated, AppName, ModifiedBy, OldValue, NewValue
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Federated Identity Credential Added
desc: Detects when a Federated Identity Credential (FIC) is added to an app registration or service principal. FIC abuse is a modern, high-impact persistence technique: attackers add a federated trust to an external identity provider (like GitHub Actions) they control, allowing token issuance without ever touching a client secret.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has_any ('Add federated identity credential', 'Certificates and secrets management')
| where tostring(TargetResources) has 'federatedIdentityCredentials'
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| extend ModifiedBy = coalesce(tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName), tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).app.displayName))
| project TimeGenerated, AppName, ModifiedBy, OperationName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Diagnostic Settings Deleted
desc: Detects deletion of diagnostic settings on Azure resources. Diagnostic settings control what telemetry flows to Log Analytics and Sentinel. Deleting them is a defense evasion technique that blinds detection for the affected resource before further malicious activity.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue =~ 'microsoft.insights/diagnosticSettings/delete'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Azure Policy Deleted or Disabled
desc: Detects deletion or disabling of Azure Policy assignments. Azure Policy often enforces security baselines (deny public IPs, require encryption, restrict regions). Removing a policy assignment can be a precursor to deploying non-compliant, insecure resources undetected.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue in ('Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments/delete', 'Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments/write')
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| project TimeGenerated, OperationNameValue, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Conditional Access Policy Modified or Deleted
desc: Detects creation, modification or deletion of Conditional Access policies. CA policies enforce MFA, block legacy auth and restrict risky sign-ins. Unauthorized changes here are one of the highest-impact defense evasion techniques in Entra ID, potentially disabling MFA enforcement tenant-wide.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has_any ('Add conditional access policy', 'Update conditional access policy', 'Delete conditional access policy')
| extend PolicyName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| extend ModifiedBy = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, PolicyName, ModifiedBy, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Defender for Cloud Alert Suppression Created
desc: Detects creation of Microsoft Defender for Cloud alert suppression rules. Suppression rules silently dismiss future alerts matching specific criteria. An attacker with sufficient access can create a broad suppression rule to hide their own future activity from the security team.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue has 'Microsoft.Security/alertsSuppressionRules'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| project TimeGenerated, OperationNameValue, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: NSG Open Inbound Rule Added
desc: Detects new Network Security Group rules that allow inbound traffic from any source (0.0.0.0/0 or Internet tag) on any port or sensitive management ports (22, 3389, 445). This is a classic technique to expose a resource to the internet for later exploitation.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue =~ 'Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/securityRules/write'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| extend RuleProps = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(Properties).requestbody))
| extend SourceAddressPrefix = tostring(RuleProps.properties.sourceAddressPrefix)
| extend DestPortRange = tostring(RuleProps.properties.destinationPortRange)
| extend Direction = tostring(RuleProps.properties.direction)
| extend Access = tostring(RuleProps.properties.access)
| where Direction == 'Inbound' and Access == 'Allow'
| where SourceAddressPrefix in ('*', '0.0.0.0/0', 'Internet')
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, DestPortRange, SourceAddressPrefix
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Key Vault Secret and Key Enumeration
desc: Detects high-volume list/enumeration operations against Azure Key Vault (SecretList, KeyList, CertificateList). Mass enumeration of vault contents from a single identity is a reconnaissance step commonly seen before targeted secret retrieval in a credential access attack chain.
kql:
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResourceProvider == 'MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT'
| where OperationName in ('SecretList', 'KeyList', 'CertificateList')
| summarize ListOps = count() by CallerIPAddress, identity_claim_upn_s, Resource, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where ListOps > 20
| order by ListOps desc

name: First-Time Key Vault Secret Access
desc: Compares today's Key Vault secret GET operations against a 30-day baseline of access patterns per caller and vault. A caller retrieving a secret from a vault they have never accessed before is a strong signal of either lateral movement or a compromised identity exploring new resources.
kql:
let Baseline = AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
| where ResourceProvider == 'MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT'
| where OperationName == 'SecretGet'
| distinct identity_claim_upn_s, Resource;
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResourceProvider == 'MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT'
| where OperationName == 'SecretGet'
| where isnotempty(identity_claim_upn_s)
| join kind=leftanti (Baseline) on identity_claim_upn_s, Resource
| project TimeGenerated, identity_claim_upn_s, Resource, CallerIPAddress, requestUri_s
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: VM Extension Silently Installed
desc: Detects installation of VM extensions, especially CustomScriptExtension and RunCommand which allow arbitrary code execution on a virtual machine. Attackers with Contributor access to a VM (without needing OS-level credentials) can use extensions to run commands, install backdoors or exfiltrate data.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue =~ 'Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| extend ExtensionProps = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(Properties).requestbody))
| extend ExtensionType = tostring(ExtensionProps.properties.type)
| where ExtensionType has_any ('CustomScript', 'RunCommand', 'DSC')
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, ExtensionType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Automation Runbook Created or Modified
desc: Detects creation or modification of Azure Automation runbooks. Automation accounts often hold powerful managed identities with subscription-wide permissions. A newly created or modified runbook can be used as a persistence and execution mechanism that runs on a schedule under a privileged identity.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue has_any ('Microsoft.Automation/automationAccounts/runbooks/write', 'Microsoft.Automation/automationAccounts/runbooks/draft/write')
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Mass Azure Resource Deletion
desc: Detects a high volume of resource delete operations from a single caller within a short time window. Mass deletion of resources is a classic impact technique used in the final stage of an attack, often to destroy evidence or cause maximum business disruption before detection.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationNameValue endswith '/delete'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| summarize DeleteCount = count(), Resources = make_set(ResourceId, 20) by Caller, CallerIpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m)
| where DeleteCount > 15
| order by DeleteCount desc

name: Subscription Ownership Transfer
desc: Detects Azure subscription ownership transfer requests and acceptances. Transferring subscription ownership hands full control (including billing) to a different account or tenant. Any unexpected transfer request is a critical event requiring immediate verification, as it can be used to hijack an entire subscription.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue has_any ('Microsoft.Subscription/transfer', 'Microsoft.Subscription/acceptOwnership', 'transferSubscription')
| project TimeGenerated, OperationNameValue, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ActivityStatusValue, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Sign-In After Long Dormancy
desc: Detects successful sign-ins from accounts with no sign-in activity in the preceding 60 days. Dormant account reactivation is a common pattern in account takeover: attackers target stale accounts that owners rarely check, reducing the chance of the compromise being noticed quickly.
kql:
let Lookback = 90d;
let DormancyThresholdDays = 60;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ResultType == '0'
| order by UserPrincipalName, TimeGenerated asc
| serialize
| extend PrevSignIn = prev(TimeGenerated), PrevUser = prev(UserPrincipalName)
| where UserPrincipalName == PrevUser
| extend GapDays = datetime_diff('day', TimeGenerated, PrevSignIn)
| where GapDays >= DormancyThresholdDays
| project UserPrincipalName, PreviousSignIn = PrevSignIn, ReactivationSignIn = TimeGenerated, GapDays, IPAddress
| order by GapDays desc

name: Credential-Named Files in SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams
desc: Cloud half of the credential file sweep. Finds files whose names suggest credentials across SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams file operations. Groups by file rather than event so you get a remediation list, not an event log. DistinctUsers is the column that matters: nine people opening the same Service Accounts.xlsx is a finding.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
let CredentialTerms = @"(?i)(password|passwrd|passwd|pwd|passcode|credential|creds|logins|secret|apikey|api[_\- ]key|privatekey|id_rsa)";
let BenignTerms = @"(?i)(compass|passport|passenger|passive|passage|bypass|encompass|surpass|secretar|secret santa|passwordless|password[_\- ]?polic|password[_\- ]?manager|password[_\- ]?expir|(reset|change|forgot)[_\- ]?password|password[_\- ]?(reset|change)|credential[_\- ]?guard)";
let DocExtensions = dynamic(["txt","csv","xls","xlsx","xlsm","doc","docx","rtf","one","md","json","yaml","yml","xml","ini","cfg","conf","env","ps1","bat","sql","pdf","pem","ppk","key","rdp","bak"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where RecordType == "SharePointFileOperation"
| where UserId !~ "app@sharepoint"
| where isnotempty(SourceFileName)
| where SourceFileName matches regex CredentialTerms
| where not(SourceFileName matches regex BenignTerms)
| where SourceFileExtension in~ (DocExtensions)
| extend Estate = iff(Site_Url has "/personal/", "OneDrive", "SharePoint")
| extend TeamsChatFile = SourceRelativeUrl has "Microsoft Teams Chat Files"
| extend OwnerPath = extract(@"/personal/([^/]+)", 1, tolower(Site_Url))
| summarize
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
    Touches = count(),
    DistinctUsers = dcount(UserId),
    TouchedBy = make_set(UserId, 25),
    Operations = make_set(Operation, 10),
    ClientIPs = make_set(ClientIP, 10)
  by SourceFileName, SourceFileExtension, Estate, TeamsChatFile, OwnerPath, Site_Url, SourceRelativeUrl
| extend FullPath = strcat(Site_Url, SourceRelativeUrl, "/", SourceFileName)
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, SourceFileName, SourceFileExtension, Estate, TeamsChatFile,
          OwnerPath, DistinctUsers, TouchedBy, Touches, Operations, ClientIPs, FullPath
| sort by DistinctUsers desc, LastSeen desc

name: Credential-Named Files That Have Been Shared
desc: The sharpest end of the credential file problem. Surfaces share operations against files whose names suggest credentials, ranked by share scope. Anonymous links come first because they need no authentication at all, then external recipients, then organization-wide links, then named internal shares. A row showing AnonymousLinkUsed against Logins.xlsx is an incident.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
let CredentialTerms = @"(?i)(password|passwrd|passwd|pwd|passcode|credential|creds|logins|secret|apikey|api[_\- ]key|privatekey|id_rsa)";
let BenignTerms = @"(?i)(compass|passport|passenger|passive|passage|bypass|encompass|surpass|secretar|secret santa|passwordless|password[_\- ]?polic|password[_\- ]?manager|password[_\- ]?expir|(reset|change|forgot)[_\- ]?password|password[_\- ]?(reset|change)|credential[_\- ]?guard)";
let ShareOperations = dynamic(["AnonymousLinkCreated","AnonymousLinkUsed","SecureLinkCreated","AddedToSecureLink","SharingInvitationCreated","SharingSet","CompanyLinkCreated","SharingLinkCreated","SharingLinkUpdated"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where RecordType in ("SharePointSharingOperation", "SharePointFileOperation")
| where Operation in (ShareOperations)
| where isnotempty(SourceFileName)
// Regex is used because file names have no word boundaries to tokenize on
| where SourceFileName matches regex CredentialTerms
| where not(SourceFileName matches regex BenignTerms)
| extend ShareScope = case(
      Operation startswith "Anonymous", "Anyone with the link",
      TargetUserOrGroupType in ("Guest", "Partner"), "External recipient",
      Operation startswith "Company", "Anyone in the organization",
      "Named internal recipient")
| extend ScopeRank = case(
      Operation startswith "Anonymous", 1,
      TargetUserOrGroupType in ("Guest", "Partner"), 2,
      Operation startswith "Company", 3,
      4)
| project TimeGenerated, ScopeRank, ShareScope, Sharer = UserId, Operation,
          SourceFileName, SourceFileExtension, SharedWith = TargetUserOrGroupName,
          TargetUserOrGroupType, SharingType, Site_Url, SourceRelativeUrl, ClientIP, UserAgent
| sort by ScopeRank asc, TimeGenerated desc

name: Privileged Service Principal Permission Grant and Anomalous Sign-In Spike
desc: Monitors for sensitive Entra ID app role grants to service principals, followed within 24 hours by an anomalous surge in sign-in activity. This behavior is a common indicator of an adversary using newly acquired permissions for large scale data access or exfiltration.
kql:
// Privileged app role grant followed by a service principal sign-in spike.
// Tune SensitivePermissions, SpikeMultiplier and MinHourlySignIns.
// Correlation uses ServicePrincipalName, not AppId. Two service principals with the same display name are merged.
let LookbackWindow = 30d;
let BaselineWindowStart = bin(ago(9d), 1h);
let BaselineWindowEnd = bin(ago(2d), 1h);
let MinHourlySignIns = 10;
let SpikeMultiplier = 5;
let SensitivePermissions = dynamic([
    "RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory",
    "Application.ReadWrite.All",
    "Directory.ReadWrite.All",
    "Mail.ReadWrite",
    "Sites.FullControl.All",
    "User.ReadWrite.All"
]);
let FirstPartyAppIdExclusions = dynamic([
    "00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000",
    "00000002-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000",
    "00000003-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000",
    "00000002-0000-0000-c000-000000000000",
    "00000004-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000",
    "00000006-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000"
]);
let FirstPartyNameExclusions = dynamic([
    "Skype for Business Online",
    "Microsoft Office 365 Portal",
    "Microsoft Graph",
    "Office 365 Exchange Online",
    "Office 365 SharePoint Online",
    "Azure Active Directory"
]);
let PrivilegedGrants = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackWindow)
| where Category =~ "ApplicationManagement" and OperationName =~ "Add app role assignment to service principal"
| mv-expand TargetResource = TargetResources
| where TargetResource.type =~ "ServicePrincipal"
| extend ServicePrincipalName = tostring(TargetResource.displayName)
| where ServicePrincipalName !in~ (FirstPartyNameExclusions)
| mv-expand modifiedProperty = TargetResource.modifiedProperties
| where tostring(modifiedProperty.displayName) =~ "AppRole.Value"
| extend GrantedPermission = trim(@'["\s]+', tostring(modifiedProperty.newValue))
| where GrantedPermission in (SensitivePermissions)
| project GrantTime = TimeGenerated, ServicePrincipalName, GrantedPermission;
let HourlyBins = range TimeBin from BaselineWindowStart to BaselineWindowEnd step 1h;
let BaselineServicePrincipals = AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
| where TimeGenerated between (BaselineWindowStart .. BaselineWindowEnd)
| where AppId !in (FirstPartyAppIdExclusions)
| distinct ServicePrincipalName;
let BaselineActivity = AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
| where TimeGenerated between (BaselineWindowStart .. BaselineWindowEnd)
| where AppId !in (FirstPartyAppIdExclusions)
| summarize HourlySignIns = count() by ServicePrincipalName, TimeBin = bin(TimeGenerated, 1h);
let Baseline = BaselineServicePrincipals
| extend dummy = 1
| join kind=inner (HourlyBins | extend dummy = 1) on dummy
| project ServicePrincipalName, TimeBin
| join kind=leftouter BaselineActivity on ServicePrincipalName, TimeBin
| extend HourlySignIns = coalesce(HourlySignIns, 0)
| summarize AvgHourly = avg(HourlySignIns) by ServicePrincipalName;
let Spikes = AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackWindow)
| where AppId !in (FirstPartyAppIdExclusions)
| summarize HourlySignIns = count() by ServicePrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| join kind=inner Baseline on ServicePrincipalName
| where HourlySignIns > AvgHourly * SpikeMultiplier and HourlySignIns >= MinHourlySignIns
| project VelocityTime = TimeGenerated, ServicePrincipalName, HourlySignIns, AvgHourly;
PrivilegedGrants
| join kind=inner Spikes on ServicePrincipalName
| where VelocityTime between (GrantTime .. datetime_add('day', 1, GrantTime))
| summarize arg_min(VelocityTime, *) by ServicePrincipalName, GrantTime
| project GrantTime, ServicePrincipalName, GrantedPermission, VelocityTime, HourlySignIns, AvgHourly
| order by GrantTime desc

name: Local AI Agent Inventory
desc: Builds an inventory of the current state of local AI agents (CLI tools, desktop apps, agentic IDEs, editor extensions) discovered on onboarded endpoints. AgentsInfo stores periodic snapshots rather than one-time events, so this dedupes to the latest snapshot per agent. Only vendor-supported local agent types are discovered, so an empty result does not guarantee no local agents are running, only that none of the supported types were detected.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where Platform == "LocalAgents"
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| extend ParsedAgentData = parse_json(RawAgentInfo)
| extend
    Vendor = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.vendor),
    DeviceName = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.deviceName),
    AccountName = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.accountName),
    AccountDomain = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.accountDomain),
    RelatedProcess = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.relatedProcess),
    TrustedProcess = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.trustedProcess),
    OSPlatform = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.osPlatform)
| project Timestamp, Name, PublishedStatus, AccountName, AccountDomain, Vendor, DeviceName, OSPlatform, RelatedProcess, TrustedProcess, LifecycleStatus, AgentId
| sort by Vendor asc, Name asc

name: AI Agent Vendor Prevalence
desc: Ranks local AI agent vendors by device count across the environment. A quick way to see which AI tools have the largest footprint before deciding where to focus AI governance policy or vendor risk review.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where Platform == "LocalAgents"
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| extend Vendor = tostring(parse_json(RawAgentInfo).localAgentMetadata.vendor)
| summarize VendorCount = count() by Vendor
| sort by VendorCount desc

name: Devices Running Multiple Local AI Agents
desc: Lists endpoints hosting local AI agents ranked by agent count, with a configurable threshold to surface devices with an unusually high concentration. A single device running many different agents is worth reviewing for shadow AI sprawl or an unmanaged developer workstation accumulating tools outside policy.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
let MinAgentsPerDevice = 5;
AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where Platform == "LocalAgents"
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| extend ParsedAgentData = parse_json(RawAgentInfo)
| extend DeviceName = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.deviceName)
| summarize
    TotalAgentsOnDevice = count(),
    Agents = make_list(bag_pack("Name", Name, "PublishedStatus", PublishedStatus, "AgentId", AgentId))
    by DeviceName
| where TotalAgentsOnDevice >= MinAgentsPerDevice
| sort by TotalAgentsOnDevice desc

name: Users Running Multiple Local AI Agents (SID-Based)
desc: Groups local AI agent usage by account SID rather than account name, since account name is sometimes not populated in agent telemetry while the SID almost always is. Useful during incident response: given a compromised device or user, quickly pull every local AI agent tied to that account, including any that a lookup by name would miss.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where Platform == "LocalAgents"
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| extend ParsedAgentData = parse_json(RawAgentInfo)
| extend
    DeviceName = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.deviceName),
    AccountName = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.accountName),
    AccountSid = tostring(ParsedAgentData.localAgentMetadata.accountSid)
| summarize
    TotalAgents = count(),
    Agents = make_list(bag_pack("Name", Name, "DeviceName", DeviceName, "AgentId", AgentId))
    by AccountSid, AccountName
| sort by TotalAgents desc

name: Published Agent Without Instructions
desc: Flags published agents with missing or placeholder instructions. An agent without clear system-prompt boundaries is more exposed to prompt injection, since there is no defined behavior for it to deviate from. Known false positives include agents still in development that have not had instructions configured yet, agents intentionally built for broad or undefined use cases and internal testing or experimental agents that do not need specific behavioral instructions.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| where PublishedStatus == "Published"
| where isempty(Instructions) or Instructions == "N/A"
| project Timestamp, AgentId, Name, Platform, Owners, SharedWith, CreatedDateTime, LastPublishedDateTime

name: Agent User Added to Group
desc: Flags Entra Agent ID identities (agentType agentIDuser, agenticApp, agenticAppInstance or agentIdentityBlueprintPrincipal) added as a member of a group, using the documented agentType field Microsoft now stamps on AuditLogs "Add member to group" events. Agent User objects carry userType=="Member", the same shape as a human account, so a dynamic group built for people can silently absorb an agent identity along with whatever licenses, roles or app permissions that group confers. MITRE ATT&CK: T1098 (Account Manipulation), T1098.003 (Additional Cloud Roles). SOC action: check whether the group is dynamic and, if so, review its membership rule for an unintended match; confirm with the group/app owner whether agent membership was deliberate; if not, remove the agent and review what access it inherited. Known limitation: while Entra Agent ID is in preview, agentType/blueprintId population is inconsistent across tenants, so an empty result is not proof no agent joined a group. It only means this field did not catch it.
kql:
// mv-expand + type match avoids relying on undocumented TargetResources array order
// Grouped by Id (unique per audit record), not CorrelationId, so a batch/bulk add
// sharing one CorrelationId can't collapse into one row
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where Category == "GroupManagement"
| where OperationName == "Add member to group"
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend ResourceType = tostring(TargetResources.type)
| extend ResourceAgentType = tostring(TargetResources.agentType)
| extend ResourceId = tostring(TargetResources.id)
| extend ResourceUPN = tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName)
| extend ResourceDisplayName = tostring(TargetResources.displayName)
| summarize
    AddedMemberId = anyif(ResourceId, ResourceType == "User"),
    AddedMemberUPN = anyif(ResourceUPN, ResourceType == "User"),
    AddedMemberAgentType = anyif(ResourceAgentType, ResourceType == "User"),
    GroupId = anyif(ResourceId, ResourceType == "Group"),
    GroupName = anyif(ResourceDisplayName, ResourceType == "Group"),
    InitiatedByAny = any(InitiatedBy),
    EventTime = any(TimeGenerated),
    EventCorrelationId = any(CorrelationId)
    by Id
| where isnotempty(AddedMemberAgentType) and AddedMemberAgentType !in ("notAgentic", "")
| extend Initiator = coalesce(tostring(InitiatedByAny.user.userPrincipalName), tostring(InitiatedByAny.app.displayName), "unknown")
| project TimeGenerated = EventTime, GroupName, GroupId, AddedMemberUPN, AddedMemberId, AddedMemberAgentType, Initiator, CorrelationId = EventCorrelationId
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// Preview limitation: agentType/blueprintId fields may be inconsistently populated
// across tenants while Entra Agent ID is in preview -- false negatives, not just false positives.

name: Device Code Sign-In Followed by New Device Registration
desc: Correlates a successful device code sign-in with a device registration by the same user within a few hours, the pattern behind device code phishing campaigns where the victim approves a code on an attacker-controlled session and the attacker then registers a device to keep persistent access that already satisfies MFA. Two independent anomaly signals ride along on the same row rather than gating the detection: an IP mismatch between the sign-in and the registration, plus a device name whose shape does not match any naming pattern seen at least 5 times in the prior 90 days, so a corporate asset tag convention drops out of the results and only unfamiliar shapes surface. MITRE ATT&CK: T1528 (Steal Application Access Token), T1098.005 (Device Registration). SOC action: treat IpMismatch plus UnfamiliarDeviceName together as the strongest signal; check SignInApp against what device code flow the user should actually be running (CLI tools, IoT/headless devices, Teams Rooms) and if it does not match, revoke the device and the session, then force reauthentication. Known false positives: legitimate BYOD or contractor onboarding with unfamiliar naming. A new but expected device code integration (CI/CD runners, smart TVs, shared kiosks) is another source until the naming baseline has 5 samples of that shape.
kql:
let Lookback = 14d;
let CorrelationWindow = 4h;
let BaselineWindow = 90d;
let MinDevicesPerPattern = 5;
let NameShape = (s: string) {
    replace_regex(replace_regex(tolower(s), @"[a-z]+", "A"), @"[0-9]+", "9")
};
let KnownShapes = SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(BaselineWindow) .. ago(Lookback))
| extend DeviceName = tostring(DeviceDetail.displayName)
| where isnotempty(DeviceName)
| extend Shape = NameShape(DeviceName)
| summarize DeviceCount = dcount(tostring(DeviceDetail.deviceId)) by Shape
| where DeviceCount >= MinDevicesPerPattern
| distinct Shape;
let DeviceCodeSignIns = SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ResultType == 0
| where AuthenticationProtocol =~ "deviceCode" or OriginalTransferMethod =~ "deviceCodeFlow"
| extend SignInCountry = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
| extend SignInWindowEnd = TimeGenerated + CorrelationWindow
| project SignInTime = TimeGenerated, SignInWindowEnd, UserPrincipalName = tolower(UserPrincipalName),
          SignInIP = IPAddress, SignInCountry, SignInUserAgent = UserAgent, SignInApp = AppDisplayName;
let DeviceRegistrations = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where OperationName =~ "Add device"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend Actor = tolower(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName))
| extend RegIP = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| mv-expand TargetResource = TargetResources
| where tostring(TargetResource.type) =~ "Device"
| extend DeviceName = tostring(TargetResource.displayName)
| where isnotempty(Actor)
| project RegTime = TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName = Actor, DeviceName, RegIP;
DeviceCodeSignIns
| join kind=inner DeviceRegistrations on UserPrincipalName
| where RegTime between (SignInTime .. SignInWindowEnd)
| extend IpMismatch = isnotempty(RegIP) and RegIP != SignInIP
| extend Shape = NameShape(DeviceName)
| extend UnfamiliarDeviceName = Shape !in (KnownShapes)
| summarize arg_min(RegTime, *) by UserPrincipalName, DeviceName
| project SignInTime, RegTime, UserPrincipalName, DeviceName, SignInIP, RegIP,
          IpMismatch, UnfamiliarDeviceName, SignInCountry, SignInUserAgent, SignInApp
| order by RegTime desc

name: Multi-LLM Provider Voting C2 with Discord Webhook Exfil
desc: Flags a non-browser process on a device calling at least two different commercial LLM provider APIs (DeepSeek, Qwen/DashScope, Mistral, Gemini) and then reaching a Discord domain within a 15-minute window. This is the network signature behind CLOSEDQUORUM, a Windows implant reported in September 2026 that polls four LLM providers for a plurality vote on its next action (steal, inject, persist or move) then reports the decision and exfiltrates stolen credentials over a Discord webhook controlled by the operator, AES-256-GCM encrypted and base64 chunked. MITRE ATT&CK: T1071.001 (Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols) for the LLM decision channel pattern, T1567 (Exfiltration Over Web Service) for the Discord leg. SOC action: on a hit, isolate the device and dump the flagged process before touching it further, then check for the payload's actual objective alongside it: LSASS access (T1003.001), browser credential file reads (T1555.003), APC injection or process hollowing (T1055.004/.012) and new Run keys, scheduled tasks or WMI subscriptions (T1547.001/T1053.005/T1546.003). Known false positives: internal AI orchestration tools and agent frameworks (for example LangChain routers or LLM gateway and proxy services) that legitimately call several providers and post status updates to a Discord bot channel. Keep AiProviderDomains current as new providers are added to the rotation and as the threat evolves.

name: SSPR-Then-MFA-Reregistration Hunt (Storm-3068 / Storm-2949)
desc: Correlates a successful self-service password reset with an authentication method change on the same account within 60 minutes. This is the persistence step seen with Storm-2949: the actor social-engineers a helpdesk call or the user themselves into an SSPR, strips existing authentication methods (phone, email, Authenticator) and registers their own Microsoft Authenticator so the legitimate owner is locked out while the attacker keeps access. Storm-3068 chained the same account takeover pattern into Kubernetes/Azure DevOps credential theft. DeletedExistingMethod on the output row is the strongest signal. An attacker removing the owner's existing method before adding their own is not something a normal self-service reset does. MITRE ATT&CK: T1556.006 (Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication), T1098 (Account Manipulation). SOC action: for any DeletedExistingMethod hit, contact the user through a channel independent of the reset (phone call, in person, not email or Teams which the attacker may also control) to confirm the reset was theirs; if not, disable the account, revoke sessions and re-enroll MFA under helpdesk verification. Known false positives: legitimate helpdesk assisted resets paired with a genuine device replacement. A new hire onboarding flow can also trigger it, since a temporary password reset and MFA registration happen back to back inside the same hour by design.
kql:
// Successful self-service password reset followed by an authentication method change
// on the same account (Storm-3068 and Storm-2949 pattern).
let Window = 60m;
let Lookback = 1d;
let Resets = AuditLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where OperationName in ("Reset password (self-service)", "Change password (self-service)")
    | where Result == "success"
    | mv-expand TargetResources
    | where tostring(TargetResources.type) == "User"
    | extend User = tolower(tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName))
    | project ResetTime = TimeGenerated, ResetOperation = OperationName, User;
let MethodChanges = AuditLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where OperationName in ("User registered security info", "User registered all required security info", "User changed default security info", "User deleted security info", "Admin registered security info")
    | mv-expand TargetResources
    | where tostring(TargetResources.type) == "User"
    | extend User = tolower(tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName))
    | project ChangeTime = TimeGenerated, OperationName, User;
Resets
| join kind=inner MethodChanges on User
| where ChangeTime between (ResetTime .. (ResetTime + Window))
| summarize Changes = make_set(OperationName), FirstChange = min(ChangeTime) by User, ResetTime, ResetOperation
| extend DeletedExistingMethod = set_has_element(Changes, "User deleted security info")
| sort by DeletedExistingMethod desc, ResetTime desc

name: Agent Skill File (SKILL.md) Created or Changed in OneDrive/SharePoint
desc: Baseline hunting query, not an alert: surfaces every SKILL.md created or changed in OneDrive or SharePoint, the instruction files that tools like Claude Code and Copilot Cowork load and follow autonomously. A SKILL.md planted or edited by someone other than its known owner is a plausible instruction injection vector into whatever agent reads it next, closer to a supply chain concern than a classic file share alert, so the goal here is visibility into where these files exist and who is touching them, not a single confirmed malicious signal. The Tool column is a folder path guess (cowork/skills vs .claude/skills) and the exclusions for common dependency folders (node_modules, .venv, vendor, build output) are plain substring matches. Both can be renamed around, so treat this as a map of the agent skill footprint to review periodically rather than a precise detector. MITRE ATT&CK: T1195.002 (Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain), closest available mapping for this class of agent tooling abuse. MITRE ATLAS: AML.T0110 (AI Agent Tool Poisoning), the precise mapping where ATT&CK has only a supply chain approximation. SOC action: for a SKILL.md touched by an unexpected user or appearing in a shared/synced location outside an individual's own OneDrive, read its actual instructions before deciding anything. A line telling the agent to exfiltrate data, call an unfamiliar tool or ignore prior constraints is the real indicator. The file event itself is not.
kql:
// Agent skill files (SKILL.md) created or changed in OneDrive and SharePoint. Hunting query, not an alert.
// Requires the Sentinel Office 365 connector with SharePoint and OneDrive audit enabled.
// Tool labels are folder-path heuristics. Noise exclusions are substring matches and can be evaded.
let Lookback = 14d;
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where OfficeWorkload in~ ("OneDrive", "SharePoint")
| where Operation in~ ("FileUploaded", "FileModified", "FileSyncUploadedFull", "FileRenamed", "FileMoved", "FileCopied")
| where SourceFileName =~ "SKILL.md" or DestinationFileName =~ "SKILL.md"
| extend Path = tolower(strcat(tostring(SourceRelativeUrl), " ", tostring(DestinationRelativeUrl), " ", tostring(OfficeObjectId)))
| where Path !contains ".venv"
    and Path !contains "site-packages"
    and Path !contains "node_modules"
    and Path !contains "__pycache__"
    and Path !contains ".git/"
    and Path !contains "/dist/"
    and Path !contains "/build/"
    and Path !contains "/vendor/"
| extend Tool = case(
    Path contains "cowork/skills", "Copilot Cowork",
    Path contains ".claude/skills", "Claude Code",
    "Other")
| extend FolderRef = coalesce(SourceRelativeUrl, OfficeObjectId)
| project TimeGenerated, OfficeWorkload, Operation, Tool, FolderRef, SourceFileName, DestinationFileName, UserId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Azure CLI Password Spray Across Many Identities
desc: Flags a single source IP authenticating via the Azure CLI client (well-known AppId 04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46) against 20+ distinct accounts while averaging 5 or fewer attempts per account, the low-and-slow signature behind LSHIY's Azure CLI spray campaign of 81 million attempts (June 2026), which evaded lockout thresholds set per account. MITRE ATT&CK: T1110.003 (Password Spraying). SOC action: for any hit, check SuccessfulAccounts and prioritize those for forced password reset and session revocation regardless of whether conditional access blocked the sign-in, since the Azure CLI path has historically had gaps in CA coverage. Known false positives: shared CI/CD runners or automation hosts running Azure CLI against many service accounts from one egress IP. Exclude those by IP or account prefix once identified.
kql:
let azureCliAppId = "04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46";
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where AppId == azureCliAppId or AppDisplayName has "Azure CLI"
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
| summarize
    TargetedAccounts   = dcount(UserPrincipalName),
    Attempts           = count(),
    Failures           = countif(ResultType != "0"),
    Successes          = countif(ResultType == "0"),
    SucceededAccounts  = make_set_if(UserPrincipalName, ResultType == "0", 25),
    FailureCodes       = make_set(ResultType, 10),
    Countries          = make_set(Country, 5),
    FirstSeen          = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen           = max(TimeGenerated)
    by IPAddress
| extend AttemptsPerAccount = todouble(Attempts) / todouble(TargetedAccounts)
| where TargetedAccounts >= 20 and AttemptsPerAccount <= 5
| sort by Successes desc, TargetedAccounts desc

name: Successful Azure CLI Sign-In Without MFA
desc: Surfaces successful Azure CLI sign-ins that completed with single-factor authentication, meaning conditional access policies claiming to enforce MFA did not cover this client path. This is the actual compromise condition in the LSHIY campaign: 81M spray attempts only mattered where a guessed password cleared without a second factor. SOC action: treat every row as a live CA gap, not just a suspicious sign-in. Confirm the account's password was not guessed (cross-reference with the companion spray detection query) and close the policy gap for the Azure CLI/legacy auth client app, not only the individual account. MITRE ATT&CK: T1078.004 (Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts). Known false positives: break-glass or emergency access accounts intentionally excluded from CA by design. Service accounts using Azure CLI under a certificate or managed identity flow are another source, since they are legitimately exempt from interactive MFA.
kql:
let azureCliAppId = "04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46";
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where AppId == azureCliAppId or AppDisplayName has "Azure CLI"
| where ResultType == "0"
| where AuthenticationRequirement == "singleFactorAuthentication"
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
| summarize
    SignIns        = count(),
    Addresses      = dcount(IPAddress),
    AddressSample  = make_set(IPAddress, 10),
    Countries      = make_set(Country, 5),
    CAStatus       = make_set(ConditionalAccessStatus, 5),
    Resources      = make_set(ResourceDisplayName, 10),
    FirstSeen      = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen       = max(TimeGenerated)
    by UserPrincipalName
| sort by Addresses desc, SignIns desc

name: Authentication Method Registration After Failed Sign-Ins
desc: Correlates 3 or more failed sign-ins with a successful security info or authentication method registration on the same account within the following hour. Seen in UNC6671 passkey vishing: the actor phones the victim claiming to be IT, walks them through 'verifying' their account during a string of failed attempts, then has them approve or register a new authentication method that survives a later password reset. MITRE ATT&CK: T1556.006 (Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication). SOC action: call the user on a channel you control to confirm they registered the method themselves; if not, remove it immediately and check whether a passkey was added, since that persists through password resets that would normally contain a compromise. Known false positives: a user who genuinely mistypes their password a few times before successfully resetting and re-registering MFA through legitimate self-service flows.
kql:
let lookback = 14d;
let failed_signins =
    SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where ResultType != "0"
    | project UserPrincipalName, FailureTime = TimeGenerated, FailureIP = IPAddress;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where Result =~ "success"
| where OperationName contains "security info" or OperationName contains "authentication method"
| extend TargetUpn = tolower(tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName))
| extend Initiator = tolower(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName))
| where isnotempty(TargetUpn)
| join kind=inner failed_signins on $left.TargetUpn == $right.UserPrincipalName
| where FailureTime between (TimeGenerated - 1h .. TimeGenerated)
| summarize FailedAttempts = count(), FirstFailure = min(FailureTime), DistinctFailureIPs = dcount(FailureIP), FailureIPs = make_set(FailureIP, 10) by TargetUpn, Initiator, OperationName, RegistrationTime = TimeGenerated
| where FailedAttempts >= 3
| order by RegistrationTime desc

name: Bulk Deletion of Security Notification Emails
desc: Flags a mailbox where 3 or more password, passkey, sign-in or security-alert notification messages were deleted in a short span. Part of UNC6671's post-compromise cleanup, systematically removing the emails a victim would otherwise see telling them their account changed. MITRE ATT&CK: T1070.008 (Indicator Removal: Clear Mailbox Data). SOC action: check what the deleted notifications were actually about (Subjects field) and cross-reference the account against recent authentication method or password reset activity. Mailbox cleanup after a real security event is a strong persistence signal, not noise to dismiss. Known false positives: aggressive inbox rules or third-party cleanup tools some users run to declutter notification spam on their own.
kql:
let lookback = 14d;
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where ActionType in~ ("MoveToDeletedItems", "SoftDelete", "HardDelete")
| extend Subject = tolower(tostring(ObjectName))
| where Subject contains "password" or Subject contains "passkey" or Subject contains "security info" or Subject contains "sign-in" or Subject contains "multi-factor" or Subject contains "verification" or Subject contains "security alert"
| summarize DeletedNotices = count(), FirstDelete = min(Timestamp), LastDelete = max(Timestamp), Subjects = make_set(ObjectName, 10), DeleteIPs = make_set(IPAddress, 5), Clients = make_set(UserAgent, 5) by AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, Application
| where DeletedNotices >= 3
| order by LastDelete desc

name: Scripted Bulk File Access by Non-Browser User-Agent
desc: Flags an account pulling 25+ distinct files through a scripted client (python-requests, curl, PowerShell, Go-http-client, okhttp) rather than a browser or sync client. Part of UNC6671's exfiltration stage: once inside, the actor used command-line tooling to pull volumes of files at a pace no interactive user matches. SOC action: pull the full file list and check whether it spans multiple sensitive sites/libraries rather than one legitimate bulk download use case. Correlate the IP/ISP against the account's normal working location. MITRE ATT&CK: T1020 (Automated Exfiltration). Known false positives: legitimate backup, DLP, eDiscovery or migration tooling that also authenticates as a user and pulls files via script. Exclude those service accounts once identified rather than raising the threshold tenant-wide.
kql:
let lookback = 7d;
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where ActionType in~ ("FileAccessed", "FileDownloaded", "FileSyncDownloadedFull")
| where UserAgent contains "python-requests" or UserAgent contains "python-urllib" or UserAgent contains "WindowsPowerShell" or UserAgent contains "Go-http-client" or UserAgent contains "okhttp" or UserAgent contains "curl"
| summarize FileEvents = count(), DistinctFiles = dcount(ObjectId), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Clients = make_set(UserAgent, 5), SourceIPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10), Providers = make_set(Isp, 5) by AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, Application
| where DistinctFiles >= 25
| order by DistinctFiles desc

name: Computer Account Creation (Machine Account Quota Abuse)
desc: Flags accounts that look unprivileged creating computer accounts in the domain, exploiting the default MachineAccountQuota of 10 that lets any authenticated user join machines to AD unless explicitly hardened. CISA's joint red team assessment of two SOCs used this exact gap for persistence and relay setup. MITRE ATT&CK: T1136.002 (Create Account: Domain Account). SOC action: verify the creator against your actual provisioning accounts list. If it is a standard user account the finding is real, so check what the new computer object was used for next (relay, Kerberos delegation abuse) and consider setting MachineAccountQuota to 0 domain-wide. Known false positives: legitimate SCCM/MDT imaging or domain join automation accounts not yet in your provisioning allowlist. Add them to provisioning_accounts rather than ignoring the finding.
kql:
let lookback = 30d;
let provisioning_accounts = dynamic(["SCCM-JOIN$", "svc-imaging", "MDT-DEPLOY$"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where EventID == 4741
| extend Creator = tolower(SubjectAccount), CreatedAccount = tolower(TargetAccount)
| where SubjectUserName !in~ (provisioning_accounts)
| summarize
    AccountsCreated = dcount(CreatedAccount),
    Created         = make_set(CreatedAccount, 25),
    Controllers     = make_set(Computer, 5),
    FirstSeen       = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen        = max(TimeGenerated)
    by Creator
| sort by AccountsCreated desc

name: Certificate Issuance Subject Name Mismatch (ESC1)
desc: Flags a certificate request where the issued Subject Alternative Name does not contain the requester's own account name, the signature of an ESC1 misconfigured template letting any user request a certificate that authenticates as someone else. CISA's red team assessment of two SOCs exploited exactly this misconfiguration to impersonate privileged accounts. This is the exploitation companion to a template enumeration query. Enumeration shows the weakness exists and this shows it was actually used. MITRE ATT&CK: T1649 (Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates). SOC action: on a hit, treat the SubjectAltName identity as compromised immediately (its credential material is now forgeable) and revoke the issued certificate, then fix the vulnerable template's enrollment permissions and EKU settings rather than only responding to individual requests. Known false positives: none expected if your templates are correctly scoped. This specific combination (mismatched SAN, successful issuance) should not occur legitimately. Requires certificate services auditing (events 4886/4887) enabled on the CA.
kql:
let lookback = 30d;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where EventID in (4886, 4887)
| extend Requester       = tolower(extract(@'(?i)Requester:\s*([^\r\n]+)', 1, EventData)),
         Template        = extract(@'(?i)Template:\s*([^\r\n]+)', 1, EventData),
         SubjectAltName  = tolower(extract(@'(?i)Subject Alternative Name:\s*([^\r\n]+)', 1, EventData)),
         RequestId       = extract(@'(?i)Request ID:\s*([^\r\n]+)', 1, EventData)
| where isnotempty(SubjectAltName)
| extend RequesterName = tostring(split(Requester, '\\')[-1])
| where isnotempty(RequesterName)
| where not(SubjectAltName has RequesterName)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID, RequestId, Requester, Template, SubjectAltName
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

name: Directory Replication Request (DCSync)
desc: Flags a directory replication request (DS-Replication-Get-Changes / DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All) made by an account that is not a domain controller or a known Entra Connect/sync service account, the DCSync technique for pulling password hashes straight from AD without touching lsass. CISA's red team used this to harvest an AES256 hash and exchange it for a Kerberos TGT. MITRE ATT&CK: T1003.006 (OS Credential Dumping: DCSync). SOC action: treat any hit as a near-certain domain compromise. The requesting account's permissions were abused to grant replication rights it should never have had. Reset krbtgt (twice) and every credential the account could reach. Known false positives: legitimate accounts that sync AD to Entra (Azure AD Connect, Entra Cloud Sync) not yet in the exclusion list. Add them by name once confirmed rather than widening the GUID filter.
kql:
let lookback = 30d;
let replication_guids = dynamic([
    "1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2",
    "1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2",
    "89e95b76-444d-4c62-991a-0facbeda640c"]);
// Regex used for prefix matching of sync service accounts
let sync_pattern = @"(^|\\)(msol_|aad_|svc-adsync)";
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where EventID == 4662
| where ObjectType has_any ("domainDNS", "19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9")
| where Properties has_any (replication_guids)
| extend Requester = tolower(SubjectAccount)
| where not(Requester endswith "$")
| where not(Requester matches regex sync_pattern)
| summarize
    Requests    = count(),
    Controllers = make_set(Computer, 5),
    FirstSeen   = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen    = max(TimeGenerated)
    by Requester
| sort by Requests desc

name: Application Secret Added Then Used for Mailbox Access
desc: Correlates a new client secret added to an application with that application's OAuth token being used for mailbox actions (read, send, bind) within the following week. CISA's red team identified an app owner with Mail.ReadWrite, obtained their refresh token, added a new client secret and read mailbox data with the resulting token, all without ever touching the owner's own credentials. MITRE ATT&CK: T1550.001 (Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token).
